hints.content:
We want to complete $x^2\blueD{+2}x$ into a perfect square.

To do that, we should add $\left(\dfrac{\blueD{+2}}{2}\right)^2=\goldD{1}$ to it:

$x^2\blueD{+2}x+\goldD{1}=(x+1)^2$

In order to keep the expression equivalent, we add and subtract $\goldD{1}$, not forgetting the expression's constant term, $-39$:

$\begin{align}
f(x)&=x^2+2x-39
\\\\
&=x^2+2x+\goldD{1}-39-\goldD{1}
\\\\
&=(x+1)^2-39-1
\\\\
&=(x+1)^2-40
\end{align}$

In conclusion, after completing the square, the function is written as

$f(x)=(x + 1)^2 - 40$
